mainTopic: The source for the לויים' שירה and the punishment for doing another's job, and whether a voluntary communal עולה needs שירה
overview: The גמרא brings several sources for the rule that the לויים must sing (שירה) during the קרבנות. A ברייתא learns from a פסוק that a כהן and a לוי who swap jobs get מיתה, while one לוי doing another לוי's job breaks only an אזהרה. אביי says a singer who did a gatekeeper's job gets מיתה, but a ברייתא says it is only an אזהרה. The גמרא tries to show that תנאים argue about this, using a story of two sages at the Temple doors, but the story can also be read another way. Then רבי אבין asks whether a voluntary communal עולה needs שירה. Proofs from חזקיהו's offering and from the day the בית המקדש was destroyed are each pushed away. Finally, a פסוק that puts עולות next to שלמים teaches that only an עולה with a set time gets שירה, so a voluntary עולה does not.

steps.title: End of the previous proof: about matters of voice
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of an earlier proof: ה׳ answered משה about matters of 'voice', which means song.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...about matters of voice.
steps.whatsHappening: These words finish a proof that started before this section. It shows that the לויים must sing, because ה׳ answered משה, a לוי, about matters of 'voice'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word קול (voice) is read as a hint to the song of the לויים. That makes this one source for the duty of שירה during the קרבנות. The next steps bring other sources for the same rule.

keyTerms.meaning: matters of, things having to do with
voice; here it hints at song
the song the לויים sang in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: about matters of voice.
phrases.notes: This finishes a proof from just before this section: ה׳ answered משה, who was a לוי, with a command about song.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a derivation that began before this section.
steps.raayaObject: That the לויים are required to sing during the קרבנות
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word קול in the earlier פסוק, read as being about song

steps.title: רב אשי's source: trumpeters and singers as one
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי learns the duty of the לויים to sing from a פסוק in דברי הימים that puts the trumpeters and the singers together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: we learn it from here: 'It came to pass, when the trumpeters and the singers were as one, to make one sound heard.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different source for the rule that the לויים must sing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק joins the trumpeters and the singers 'as one'. Blowing the trumpets during the קרבנות is a known requirement, so the singing that goes with it is a requirement too.

keyTerms.meaning: from here; we learn it from this פסוק
trumpeters (the כהנים who blew trumpets)
singers (the לויים)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: from here:
"It came to pass, when the trumpeters were as one
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 5:13

phrases.english: with the singers, to make one sound heard."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different source for the same rule proven in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That שירה by the לויים is required
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברי הימים ב 5:13, which joins the trumpeters and the singers

steps.title: Rabbi Yonatan's source: just like you, they serve the altar
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן learns it from a פסוק that puts the לויים and the כהנים side by side: just as the כהנים serve at the מזבח, the לויים also have a job connected to the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן said: from here: 'That they not die, neither they nor you.' Just as you (the כהנים) do the service of the altar, so too they (the לויים) do a service of the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן gives a third source for the singing of the לויים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'they' and 'you' in one breath, so the גמרא compares them. The כהנים do the work at the מזבח, so the לויים must also have a job tied to the מזבח, and that job is the song that goes with the קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: the service of the altar
just as... so too... (a way of comparing two things)
neither they nor you; it links the לויים and the כהנים

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan said: from here:
"That they not die, neither they nor you" —
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:3. 'They' are the לויים and 'you' are the כהנים.

phrases.english: just as you are in the service of the altar,
so too they are in the service of the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another source for the same rule as steps 1 and 2.
steps.raayaObject: That the לויים have a required service tied to the מזבח, namely שירה
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 18:3, which compares the לויים to the כהנים

steps.title: A ברייתא on swapping jobs between כהנים and לויים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא also learns from the same פסוק as רבי יונתן. A כהן doing a לוי's job, or a לוי doing a כהן's job, gets מיתה. A לוי doing another לוי's job gets only an אזהרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: 'That they not die, neither they nor you.' You in their job, or they in your job, is punishable by death. They in their own kind of job is not punishable by death, only by a warning (a prohibition).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that reads the same פסוק as רבי יונתן and learns punishments from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that the פסוק really does treat the כהנים and the לויים as two groups with their own jobs, which backs up רבי יונתן's use of it. The ברייתא sets two levels: crossing between כהנים and לויים brings מיתה בידי שמים, while one לוי doing a different לוי's job is only a plain prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: also like this; this backs up what was just said
punished with death (מיתה בידי שמים, death at the hands of Heaven)
a warning; a prohibition without the death penalty
in theirs; doing a job that belongs to them

steps.whatToRemember: Two levels: a כהן and a לוי switching jobs means מיתה. One לוי doing another לוי's job means only an אזהרה, according to this ברייתא.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
"That they not die, neither they nor you" —
you in theirs and they in yours is punishable by death,
phrases.notes: 'You' are the כהנים and 'they' are the לויים, so this means swapping jobs between the two groups.

phrases.english: they in theirs are not punishable by death
but only by a prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יונתן's reading of the פסוק and adds rules about punishment.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יונתן's comparison of the כהנים and the לויים in במדבר 18:3
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that reads the same פסוק

steps.title: אביי: a singer who did a gatekeeper's job gets death
steps.stepSummary: אביי says there is a known tradition: a לוי singer who did his fellow's gatekeeping job is punished with מיתה. He brings a פסוק that ends 'and the stranger who comes near shall be put to death.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: we have a tradition that a singer who did gatekeeping in his fellow's place is punishable by death, as it says: 'And those who camp before the משכן to the east, before the אהל מועד... and the stranger who comes near shall be put to death.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי states a rule about a singer doing a gatekeeper's job and gives a פסוק as its source. The next steps explain how the פסוק proves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here one לוי (a singer) does another לוי's job (gatekeeping), and אביי says the punishment is מיתה. His proof rests on the word זר in the פסוק, which the גמרא now goes on to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: we hold; we have a tradition
a singer among the לויים
did gatekeeping (from שוער, a gatekeeper)
a stranger, an outsider

phrases.english: Abaye said: We hold,
a singer who did gatekeeping in his fellow's place is punishable by death,
as it is stated: "And those who camp before the Mishkan to the east,
phrases.notes: במדבר 3:38

phrases.english: before the Tent of Meeting, etc.
and the stranger who comes near shall be put to death."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתא's general rules to a specific case: a singer doing a gatekeeper's job.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A singer who did his fellow's gatekeeping job is punishable by מיתה.

steps.title: What does 'stranger' mean here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word זר in אביי's פסוק means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'stranger'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what זר means in the פסוק. This sets up the explanation that will show how אביי proves his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's whole proof depends on what זר means. If it means a non-לוי, the פסוק says nothing about a singer, so the גמרא has to pin down the meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: what is?

phrases.english: What is "stranger"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the key word in אביי's פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who the זר in במדבר 3:38 is

steps.title: It cannot mean a real outsider
steps.stepSummary: If זר meant an actual outsider (a non-לוי), the פסוק would be repeating something the Torah already wrote somewhere else.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means an actual stranger, isn't that already written once?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the simple meaning, a real outsider, and rejects it because the Torah already said that in another place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not repeat itself for no reason. A non-לוי coming near is already punished with מיתה in another פסוק, so this זר must be teaching something new.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say; it brings up a possible meaning in order to test it
actual, literal
it is already written once

phrases.english: If you say an actual stranger —
but it is already written once!
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק in במדבר 3:10, which already gives מיתה to an outsider who comes near.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules out the first possible answer to the question in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Reading זר as a real non-לוי
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would make the פסוק a repeat of something already written in another place.

steps.title: It means an outsider to that particular job
steps.stepSummary: So זר must mean someone who is an outsider to that specific job, such as a singer doing gatekeeping. That proves אביי's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, doesn't it mean a stranger to that particular service?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that זר here means someone who is a stranger to that particular job, even though he is a לוי. That backs up אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the simple meaning is already covered elsewhere, the word is read in a new way: someone outside that particular job. A singer doing a gatekeeper's work is a זר to gatekeeping, so he gets מיתה, just as אביי said.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, is it not...? (it brings the only reading left)
a stranger to that particular service

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, זר in במדבר 3:38 means a לוי who is an outsider to that particular job. So a singer who does gatekeeping gets מיתה.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not a stranger to that particular service?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the remaining reading of זר after step 7 ruled out the simple one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: זר means someone who is an outsider to that particular job, such as a singer doing gatekeeping.

steps.title: A ברייתא says a singer doing gatekeeping gets no death penalty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי with a ברייתא saying a singer who did gatekeeping, or a gatekeeper who sang, gets only an אזהרה, not מיתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged אביי: a singer who did gatekeeping, or a gatekeeper who sang, is not punished with death. It is only a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's rule from Step 5. It brings a ברייתא that says the exact opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said a singer doing a gatekeeper's job gets מיתה. This ברייתא talks about the very same case and says it is only an אזהרה. It also matches the ברייתא from Step 4: one לוי doing another לוי's job gets only an אזהרה.

keyTerms.meaning: A לוי whose job is singing in the בית המקדש
A לוי whose job is guarding the gates (gatekeeper)
A plain prohibition with no death penalty
Death penalty (here, death at the hands of Heaven)

phrases.english: They raised an objection: a singer who did gatekeeping
and a gatekeeper who sang
are not liable to death, only to a prohibition!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's rule, which Steps 5-8 had just proven from the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's tradition that a singer doing gatekeeping is punished with מיתה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא rules on the very same case and gives only an אזהרה, directly contradicting אביי.

steps.title: It is a dispute between תנאים, shown by a story at the Temple doors
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this is a dispute between תנאים. It brings a story where רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא told רבי יהושע בן חנניה, a singer, not to help close the doors.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute between תנאים. As a ברייתא says: רבי יהושע בר חנניה once went to help רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא close the Temple doors. רבי יוחנן said to him: My son, go back. You are one of the singers, not one of the gatekeepers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אביי by saying he simply follows a different תנא than the ברייתא does. It brings a story to show that תנאים really did argue about this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי is not refuted just because one ברייתא disagrees with him, as long as another תנא holds like him. In the story, one sage, a singer, came to help the gatekeepers, and the other sage sent him away. The next step explains how this story shows a dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים (sages of the משנה era)
To help or assist
Closing the doors (of the בית המקדש), a gatekeeper's job

phrases.english: It is a dispute of תנאים, as it is taught:
There was an incident with רבי יהושע בר חנניה
who went to help with closing the doors
alongside רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא.
He said to him: My son, go back,
for you are one of the singers
and not one of the gatekeepers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 9 by saying the ברייתא and אביי follow different תנאים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute between תנאים: אביי follows a different תנא than the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא reflects only one side of a dispute between תנאים. אביי can follow the other side.

steps.title: Reading the story as a dispute about מיתה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the two sages disagree: one holds the act carries מיתה, so the רבנן banned even helping; the other holds it is only an אזהרה, so there was no such ban.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this what they disagree about? One sage holds it is a death-penalty sin, so the רבנן made a decree against it. The other sage holds it is only a prohibition, so they made no decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the story proves a dispute between תנאים. It reads each sage's behavior as showing his view on מיתה versus אזהרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא would not let a singer even help, which suggests a strong extra ban by the רבנן. That fits if he holds that doing the job alone carries מיתה. רבי יהושע was ready to help, which suggests he holds it is only an אזהרה, so there was no extra ban.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that...? (the גמרא proposing a reading)
They disagree
The רבנן made a decree (an extra protective ban)
One sage holds

phrases.english: Is it not about this that they disagree:
that one sage holds it is a death-penalty sin,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא, the one who sent the singer away.

phrases.english: and so the רבנן made a decree about it,
and the other sage holds it is only a prohibition,
and so they made no decree about it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the story in Step 10 shows a dispute between תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: That תנאים disagree about whether one לוי doing another's job carries מיתה, so אביי has a תנא to follow.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבי יהושע בר חנניה and רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא at the Temple doors

steps.title: Maybe everyone agrees it is only an אזהרה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: maybe both sages agree it is only an אזהרה, and they disagree only about whether the רבנן banned even helping.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees it is only a prohibition. One sage holds that the רבנן made a decree against even helping, and the other holds the רבנן made no such decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own reading of the story. It shows the story can be explained without anyone holding of מיתה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument could be only about a rabbinic decree on helping, not about the Torah punishment. Both sages may agree that doing the job alone is only an אזהרה. If so, the story no longer shows any תנא who holds like אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
One who only helps (rather than doing the job by himself)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up doing the job alone with just helping. The Torah issue (מיתה or אזהרה) is about doing it alone. The decree here is only about helping.

phrases.english: Everyone agrees it is only a prohibition;

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: מְסַיֵּיעַ גְּזַרוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: one sage holds the רבנן made a decree even against one who helps,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: לָא גְּזַרוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: and the other holds the רבנן made no decree about him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading in Step 11 by offering a different explanation of the sages' dispute.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the story that some תנא holds of מיתה; it does not reject the story itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The dispute can be about a rabbinic decree on helping, so it does not show any disagreement about the Torah punishment.
steps.whyThisMatters: With this pushback, אביי is left again without a תנא clearly on his side against the ברייתא of Step 9.

steps.title: Does a voluntary communal burnt offering need song?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבין asks whether the לויים' שירה goes with every communal עולה, including a voluntary one, or only with the required ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין asked: Does a voluntary communal burnt offering need song, or not? The Torah says 'your burnt offerings.' Does that mean both required and voluntary ones? Or does 'your burnt offerings' mean the ones that belong to all of Israel, meaning the required ones?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. רבי אבין wants to know if a voluntary communal עולה also gets the לויים' song.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source for song with offerings is the word 'עֹלֹתֵיכֶם' (your burnt offerings). This word could include every communal עולה, required or voluntary. Or it could mean only the offerings that all of Israel must bring, which are the required ones.

keyTerms.meaning: A voluntary burnt offering brought for the community, not one it is required to bring
Needs to have the לויים' song with it
A required burnt offering, such as the daily or holiday offerings
'The Merciful One', meaning the Torah or ה׳
'Or perhaps', which introduces the second side of a question

phrases.english: Rabbi Avin asked:
Does a communal voluntary burnt offering need song
or does it not need song?
The Merciful One said 'your burnt offerings,'
phrases.notes: במדבר 10:10, the פסוק about blowing trumpets over your offerings.

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת עוֹלַת חוֹבָה וְאַחַת עוֹלַת נְדָבָה,
phrases.english: meaning both a required burnt offering and a voluntary burnt offering,
or perhaps 'your burnt offerings'
means the ones of all Israel, the Merciful One is saying?
phrases.notes: In other words, only offerings that all of Israel is required to bring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about song with offerings, after the discussion of singers and gatekeepers.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the requirement of שירה applies to a voluntary communal עולה or only to a required one.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how one word in a פסוק, 'עֹלֹתֵיכֶם', can be read broadly or narrowly, and the rest of the discussion tries to decide which reading is right.

steps.title: Proof from חזקיהו's offering with song
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק where חזקיהו commanded an עולה with song. It argues this must have been a voluntary עולה, since a required one would not need his command.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And חזקיהו said to offer the burnt offering on the altar, and when the burnt offering began, the song of ה׳ began, with trumpets and the instruments of דוד king of Israel.' What was this song for? If it was for a required burnt offering, why did they need to ask him? So it must have been for a voluntary burnt offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer רבי אבין's question from a story in דברי הימים. It argues that song was played with a voluntary עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A required offering is brought with song anyway, so nobody would need the king's permission for it. The fact that they asked חזקיהו shows this was something extra, a voluntary עולה. So a voluntary communal עולה does get song.

keyTerms.meaning: Trumpets
What was it for? What is its purpose?
To ask for permission or consult someone
'Rather, isn't it...', which introduces the conclusion of a proof

phrases.english: Come and hear:
'And Hezekiah said to offer the burnt offering on the altar,
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 29:27

phrases.aramaic: וּבְעֵת הֵחֵל הָעוֹלָה הֵחֵל שִׁיר ה׳
phrases.english: and when the burnt offering began, the song of ה׳ began
and the trumpets, together with the instruments of song
of David, king of Israel.'
This song, what was it for?
If you say it was for a required burnt offering,
why did they need to ask permission?
phrases.notes: He means: why would they need חזקיהו's command for something they always do?

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it for a voluntary burnt offering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer רבי אבין's question in favor of song for a voluntary עולה.
steps.raayaObject: That a voluntary communal עולה needs שירה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק in דברי הימים ב 29:27, where חזקיהו commanded an עולה with song.

steps.title: רב יוסף: it was the required ראש חודש offering
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rejects the proof. It was the required עולה of ראש חודש, and they asked חזקיהו only whether that day had been set as ראש חודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: No, it was the burnt offering of ראש חודש. They were unsure whether ראש חודש had been set on its proper day, which would decide whether the offering should be brought or not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף pushes back on the proof. He says the offering in the story could have been a required one after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the question 'why ask permission?'. רב יוסף gives a different reason for asking: they were not sure the day was ראש חודש. If it was, the required ראש חודש עולה would be brought, so the story says nothing about voluntary offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: The required extra burnt offering brought on ראש חודש
Was set or declared, here by בית דין
On its proper time, the earlier possible day
So that it should be offered

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: No,
it was the burnt offering of the New Moon,
and they were unsure
whether the New Moon had been set on its proper day
so that it should be offered, or not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 14 by explaining the story differently.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the story. It does not decide רבי אבין's question either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The request for permission can be explained without a voluntary offering: they were unsure whether the day was ראש חודש.
steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not saying voluntary offerings have no song. He is only saying this story cannot prove that they do.

steps.title: אביי: the date was the 16th, not ראש חודש
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף. The פסוקים place this event on the sixteenth of the first month, so it could not have been ראש חודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: How can you say that? It is written: 'On the sixteenth day of the first month...' and then 'And חזקיהו said to offer the burnt offering on the altar'!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's answer from the dates in the same story. The גמרא is setting up the next move in the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's answer only works if the day was ראש חודש. But the פסוקים tie this event to the sixteenth of the month, which is nowhere near ראש חודש. So רב יוסף's explanation seems impossible, and the proof for voluntary offerings comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Can you really say that?', a sign that an answer is being challenged
'But isn't it written...', which brings a פסוק as a challenge
The first month, ניסן

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
And can you really say that?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכְתִיב ״בַּיּוֹם שִׁשָּׁה עָשָׂר לַחֹדֶשׁ הָרִאשׁוֹן וְגוֹ׳״,
phrases.english: But isn't it written: 'On the sixteenth day of the first month, etc.'
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 29:17. The sixteenth of a month can't be ראש חודש.

phrases.english: and then 'And Hezekiah said to offer the burnt offering on the altar'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וּמִי מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יוסף's rejection in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that the offering in חזקיהו's story was the ראש חודש עולה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוקים date the event to the sixteenth of the first month, so that day could not have been ראש חודש.

steps.title: The Question Was About the עומר Lamb
steps.stepSummary: רמי בריה דרב ייבא answers אביי. On the sixteenth, the required lamb that comes with the עומר is brought. They asked חזקיהו whether ראש חודש ניסן had been set on time, which would decide whether the lamb should be brought that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רמי בריה דרב ייבא said: They were asking about the lamb that comes with the עומר. Was ראש חודש set at its proper time, so that the lamb should be offered today, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer that fits אביי's date of the sixteenth. The offering was the required lamb of the עומר, and the question was whether today was really the sixteenth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי showed that the day could not be ראש חודש. רמי keeps the idea that it was a required offering but picks one that does belong on the sixteenth. Since the offering was required, the proof that a voluntary עולה gets שירה still falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: The required communal lamb עולה brought together with the עומר on the sixteenth of ניסן
They were asking about, or were unsure about
Set or fixed (the start of the month)
At its proper time

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָמֵי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יֵיבָא:
phrases.english: Rather, Rami son of Rav Yeiva said:
The lamb that comes with the omer
is what they were asking about,
was the New Moon set at its proper time
so that it should be offered, or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָמֵי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יֵיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge by moving the offering from ראש חודש to the עומר lamb of the sixteenth
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of which required offering was meant
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יוסף's reading, that it was the ראש חודש offering, cannot work on the sixteenth
steps.terutzMaskana: It was the required עומר lamb, and they asked whether the date was correct

steps.title: They Could Have Counted From פסח
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא challenges רמי. There was no reason to be unsure of the date. They could simply count from the day the פסח was brought and the night the מצה was eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אויא challenged it: Let them look at when the פסח was done and when the מצה was eaten!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אויא attacks רמי's answer. The people already knew the date from the פסח and מצה, so they had no need to ask חזקיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסח is on the fourteenth, and the מצה is eaten that night. Two days later is obviously the sixteenth. So a doubt about whether today was the sixteenth makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Challenges or objects
The קרבן פסח, brought on the fourteenth of ניסן
מצה, eaten on the first night of פסח

phrases.english: Rav Avya challenged it:
But let them see when the Paschal offering was done,
and when the matza was eaten!
phrases.notes: Counting from those days would already tell them which day was the sixteenth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רמי's explanation from step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי's claim that they were unsure whether it was the sixteenth
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The date was easy to figure out from the פסח and the מצה, so there was nothing to ask

steps.title: Asking Was Only a Sign of Respect
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the people were not really unsure about anything. They asked חזקיהו out of respect, the way a שליח ציבור asks the community's permission before leading the prayers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: It is just like the prayer leader of the community, who asks permission.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains that the question to חזקיהו was not a real doubt. It was a respectful formality.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אויא's challenge assumed that people only ask when they need information. רב אשי says that asking can also be a way of showing honor. A שליח ציבור asks permission even though everyone already wants him to lead.

keyTerms.meaning: Just like, the same as
The prayer leader, the שליח ציבור
Asks permission or consults

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
It is just like the prayer leader of the community
who asks permission.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַשְּׁלִיחָא דְצִיבּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אויא by saying the asking was a formality, not a real doubt
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the asking as an act of respect
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Asking חזקיהו means they really did not know the answer
steps.terutzMaskana: They asked only to honor the king, like a שליח ציבור asking permission

steps.title: Even an Ordinary Required Offering Fits
steps.stepSummary: Once asking can be a mere sign of respect, the offering in the פסוק could be any regular required עולה. So the proof from חזקיהו that a voluntary עולה gets שירה is completely gone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have come to this, you can even say it was a required עולה, just like the prayer leader who asks permission.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the wider result of רב אשי's answer. Any required offering fits the story, so the proof from step 14 no longer works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 argued that a required עולה would not need the king's command. But if commanding is only a matter of respect, a required עולה can also come with a command. That means we no longer need to look for a special date or a special offering.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have arrived at this explanation
You can even say
A required (obligatory) עולה, such as the daily תמיד

steps.whatToRemember: The story of חזקיהו cannot prove that a voluntary communal עולה gets שירה, because asking the king could just be a sign of respect. The גמרא goes on to try another proof, and step 34 finally answers the question.

phrases.english: Now that you have come to this,
you can even say it was a required burnt offering,
just like the prayer leader of the community who asks permission.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands רב אשי's answer to cover any required offering
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The proof from חזקיהו falls away completely, so רבי אבין's question still needs another source; steps 33–34 provide it.

steps.title: A New Proof Begins: Good Days and Bad Days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new attempt to answer רבי אבין's question. It quotes רבי יוסי: good things are brought about on a good day, and bad things on a bad day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יוסי says: Good things are brought about on a good day, and bad things on a bad day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new proof by quoting the opening of רבי יוסי's ברייתא. The actual proof about שירה comes in the next part of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the חזקיהו proof failed, the גמרא tries a different source. This line is only the general rule that opens the ברייתא. The details that bear on שירה with a voluntary עולה come next.

keyTerms.meaning: Bring about, cause to happen
Something good or fortunate
A good, fortunate day
A bad, unfortunate day

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Rabbi Yosei says:
Good things are brought about on a good day,
and bad things on a bad day.
phrases.notes: Here חובה means something bad, not an obligation. The part that bears on שירה comes later in this ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof failed, the גמרא starts a new proof for רבי אבין's question
steps.raayaObject: Whether שירה goes with a voluntary communal עולה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי יוסי, which continues past this line

steps.title: The day the first Temple was destroyed
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא describes the day the first בית המקדש fell. It was תשעה באב, a Sunday, the year after שמיטה, and the week of משמר יהויריב. The לויים were in the middle of singing a פסוק about punishment when the enemy broke in. The same happened at the second בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: When the first בית המקדש was destroyed, that day was תשעה באב. It was מוצאי שבת, the year after a שמיטה year, and the week of the משמר of יהויריב. The כהנים and לויים were standing on their דוכן singing. What did they sing? 'He brought their wickedness back on them, and in their evil He will cut them off.' They did not manage to finish with 'ה׳ our God will cut them off' before the nations came in and conquered them. The same thing happened at the second בית המקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues quoting the ברייתא of רבי יוסי from the last step, describing the day the first בית המקדש was destroyed. This is the story the גמרא will use to try to answer רבי אבין's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail is that the לויים were singing שירה on their platform on that day. The גמרא will soon ask what offering this singing could have gone with. The list of 'bad' dates (תשעה באב, after שבת, after שמיטה) shows רבי יוסי's idea that bad things happen on bad days.

keyTerms.meaning: The Ninth of Av, the day of the Temples' destruction
The year right after the שמיטה year
The week when the כהנים of the family-group יהויריב served
The platform the לויים stood on to sing

phrases.english: They said: When the Temple was destroyed the first time,
that day was the Ninth of Av,
and it was the day after Shabbos,
phrases.notes: So it was a Sunday. Keep this in mind, because it matters in step 26.

phrases.english: and it was the year after a Shemitah year,
and it was the week of the Yehoyariv priestly group,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיוּ כֹּהֲנִים וּלְוִיִּם עוֹמְדִים עַל דּוּכָנָן
phrases.english: and the Kohanim and Levites were standing on their platform
and singing song.
And what song did they sing?
'And He brought back upon them their wickedness,'
phrases.notes: תהלים 94:23

phrases.english: and in their evil He will cut them off,'
and they did not manage to say 'ה׳ our God will cut them off'
before the nations came and conquered them.
And so too at the second Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא of רבי יוסי begun in step 21, giving the story the proof will be built on.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a voluntary communal עולה gets שירה (רבי אבין's question)
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: the לויים were singing on the day the first בית המקדש was destroyed

steps.title: The singing must have been over a voluntary offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what offering this singing went with. It could not be a required עולה, because the תמיד had already stopped on שבעה עשר בתמוז. So it must have been a voluntary עולה, which would prove that a voluntary עולה gets שירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was this song for? If you say it was for a required burnt offering, was there one? The daily offering stopped on the seventeenth of Tammuz! So it must have been for a voluntary burnt offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the proof out of the ברייתא. Since no required offering was being brought, the song must have gone with a voluntary עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning works by ruling things out. שירה goes with a קרבן, and the required offerings had stopped three weeks earlier. That leaves only a voluntary עולה, so a voluntary עולה must get שירה. This would answer רבי אבין's question.

keyTerms.meaning: A required burnt offering
A voluntary burnt offering
The daily communal offering brought every morning and afternoon
The 17th of Tammuz, when the תמיד stopped before the destruction
What was its purpose? What was it for?

phrases.english: This song, what was it for?
If you say it was for a required burnt offering, was there one?
On the seventeenth of Tammuz the daily offering stopped!
So is it not for a voluntary burnt offering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the actual proof out of the ברייתא quoted in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: A voluntary communal עולה gets שירה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The singing on תשעה באב, when the תמיד had already stopped

steps.title: If there were no animals, how was a voluntary offering brought?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. The required offerings stopped because there were no animals. So why would a voluntary offering be possible when a required one was not?
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think that? What is different about a required offering, that it was not brought, and what is different about a voluntary offering, that it was brought?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof it just built. If there were no animals for the required offerings, there should be none for voluntary ones either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depends on a voluntary עולה actually being brought on that day. But whatever stopped the תמיד, a lack of animals, should have stopped voluntary offerings too. If no offering was brought at all, there was nothing for the song to go with, and the proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Can you really think that? It opens a challenge to an idea.
What is the difference?

phrases.english: And can you really think that?!

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא דְּעוֹלַת חוֹבָה דְּלָא הֲוַאי,
phrases.english: What is different about a required offering, that it was not brought,
and what is different about a voluntary offering, that it was brought?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִסְבְּרַאּ מַאי שְׁנָא דְּעוֹלַת חוֹבָה דְּלָא הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in step 23 that a voluntary עולה was being brought.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that a voluntary עולה was brought on תשעה באב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The lack of animals that stopped the תמיד should have stopped voluntary offerings too

steps.title: A young bull just happened to come their way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a בן בקר happened to come into their hands. A bull cannot be used for the תמיד, which needs a lamb, so they brought it as a voluntary עולה. The proof stands for now.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is not hard. A young bull just happened to come their way by chance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the proof. A bull came their way by chance, and since it could not serve as a תמיד, it was offered as a voluntary עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תמיד must be a lamb, so a bull could not fill that role. A stray bull could still be offered as a voluntary עולה. So it makes sense that a voluntary offering was brought while the required one was not, and the proof that a voluntary עולה gets שירה is back in place.

keyTerms.meaning: That is not difficult. It opens an answer.
A young bull
Just by chance

phrases.english: That is not difficult:
a young bull, just by chance,
is what happened to come their way.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא: בֶּן בָּקָר אַקְרַאי בְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24 and saves the proof of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the facts: an animal unfit for the תמיד was available
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No animals at all were available, so no offering could have been brought
steps.terutzMaskana: A stray bull, unfit for the תמיד, was brought as a voluntary עולה, and the לויים sang over it

steps.title: They were singing the wrong day's song
steps.stepSummary: רבא, or some say רב אשי, points out a problem with the ברייתא. The destruction was on a Sunday, and Sunday's song is 'לה׳ הארץ ומלואה'. But 'וישב עליהם את אונם' comes from Wednesday's song.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said, and some say רב אשי: Can you really think that? The song for that day is 'The earth and all that fills it belong to ה׳.' And 'He brought back upon them their wickedness' is in the song for Wednesday!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא (or רב אשי) finds a contradiction in the story. The פסוק the לויים were singing does not belong to Sunday's song at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each day of the week had its own fixed תהלים chapter for the Temple song. Since it was מוצאי שבת, a Sunday, the song should have been תהלים 24. The פסוק quoted is from תהלים 94, Wednesday's song. So what they were saying cannot have been the regular song over a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: The song set for that day of the week
The song for Wednesday, the fourth day of the week

phrases.english: Rava said, and some say Rav Ashi:
And can you really think that?
The song of that day is 'The earth and all that fills it belong to ה׳,'
phrases.notes: תהלים 24:1. The ברייתא said it was מוצאי שבת, so this is Sunday's song.

phrases.english: and 'He brought back upon them their wickedness'
is in the song for Wednesday!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אָשֵׁי: וְתִסְבְּרָא, שִׁירָה דְּיוֹמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new attack on the whole proof by questioning whether this was really Temple שירה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the לויים' words in the ברייתא were the official שירה over a קרבן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The quoted פסוק is from Wednesday's song, but the day was a Sunday

steps.title: It was only a lament, not Temple song
steps.stepSummary: רבא's conclusion: the words were not official שירה at all. They were a lament that came into the לויים' mouths. So the story proves nothing about a voluntary עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it was just a lament that came into their mouths.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא (or רב אשי) finishes his point. The לויים were not singing the Temple song but simply crying out a lament, so the proof is gone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the words were only a spontaneous lament, there was no שירה over any קרבן that day. Then nothing can be learned about whether a voluntary עולה needs שירה. The whole proof from steps 23 and 25 collapses, so the גמרא will need a different source; steps 33–34 provide it.

keyTerms.meaning: A lament, a cry of mourning
Fell into their mouths, came out of them on its own

steps.whatToRemember: The story of the destruction cannot prove that a voluntary עולה gets שירה. The לויים were only saying a lament, not the official song over a קרבן.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the בן בקר answer in step 25 still holds the proof up. Even if a bull was offered, רבא shows the words were not the song for any offering, so the proof falls anyway.

phrases.english: Rather, it was just a lament
phrases.notes: This is still רבא (or רב אשי) talking, finishing the point he started.

phrases.english: that came into their mouths.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִילְיָיא בְּעָלְמָא הוּא דִּנְפַל לְהוּ בְּפוּמַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from step 26's contradiction and rejects the proof of step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the entire proof from the destruction story
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The words the לויים said were a spontaneous lament, not the official שירה over a קרבן, so they show nothing about voluntary offerings
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: No proof from the destruction story; רבי אבין's question is answered only later, in steps 33–34.

steps.title: But they were standing on their platform
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's answer. The ברייתא says the לויים were standing on their דוכן, the place where official שירה is sung.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא teaches that they were 'standing on their platform'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that the לויים' words were only a lament. The ברייתא describes them standing on the דוכן, which sounds like official שירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The דוכן is where the לויים stand to sing with the offerings. If they were standing there, it seems they were doing real שירה for an offering. That would bring back the proof that a voluntary עולה gets שירה.

keyTerms.meaning: The platform near the מזבח where the לויים stood to sing
The Levites, who sang the שירה in the בית המקדש
'But isn't it…?' This opens a challenge

phrases.english: But it teaches 'they were standing on their platform'!
phrases.notes: This is quoting the ברייתא about the day the בית המקדש was destroyed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's rejection in step 27, which said the words were only a lament
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the לויים were not singing official שירה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Standing on the דוכן is the setting of official שירה, so the words should count as שירה for an offering.

steps.title: Songs may be said on the platform even without an offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with ריש לקיש: the לויים may say songs on the דוכן even when there is no offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows ריש לקיש, who said: one may recite songs even when it is not for an offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that standing on the דוכן does not prove there was an offering. According to ריש לקיש, the לויים can say songs there even without one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that the דוכן is only used for שירה with an offering. ריש לקיש says the לויים may also say songs there with no offering at all. So רבא's reading still works: they stood on the דוכן, but it was not שירה for a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Not connected to an offering
Recites. Here it means saying songs
'In line with', following someone's opinion

phrases.english: It is like ריש לקיש, who said:
One may recite songs not for an offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28
steps.terutzResolutionType: Bringing an outside opinion that removes the assumption behind the question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Standing on the דוכן means official שירה for an offering
steps.terutzMaskana: Songs may be said on the דוכן even without an offering, so the story still proves nothing

steps.title: Then sing for a voluntary עולה too
steps.stepSummary: If the לויים may sing on the דוכן even with no offering, they should also be able to sing for a voluntary עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let them also say songs with a voluntary עולה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on ריש לקיש's idea. If singing with no offering is allowed, why not sing with a voluntary עולה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Singing with no offering at all seems like more of a stretch than singing with a voluntary offering. So if the first is allowed, the second should surely be allowed too. The question is why we would ever say a voluntary עולה does not get שירה.

keyTerms.meaning: A voluntary burnt offering, brought by choice and not as a requirement
'If so.' This opens a challenge based on the last answer
Let him say. Here it means let them sing

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, בְּעוֹלַת נְדָבָה נָמֵי לֵימָא?
phrases.english: If so, let them also recite songs with a voluntary burnt offering?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, בְּעוֹלַת נְדָבָה נָמֵי לֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 29
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's rule that songs may be said without an offering
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If songs are allowed with no offering, they should certainly be allowed with a voluntary עולה.

steps.title: It could lead to a mistake
steps.stepSummary: Singing for a voluntary עולה could cause a mishap, so it is not done.
steps.simpleTranslation: A mishap could come out of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that singing for a voluntary עולה could lead to a bad mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the לויים sang as an option with a voluntary עולה, people might start to think שירה is optional with a required עולה too. Singing with no offering does not cause this confusion, because nobody would mix it up with the real שירה of a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'ruin'. Here it means a mishap or a mistake
Comes out of it, results from it
The official song of the לויים that goes with the offerings

phrases.english: A mishap would come out of it.
phrases.notes: The worry is that people would treat שירה with required offerings as optional too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 30
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical concern that blocks the comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If singing without an offering is allowed, singing with a voluntary עולה should be allowed too
steps.terutzMaskana: Optional singing with a voluntary עולה could make people treat required שירה as optional
steps.whatToRemember: The story of the חורבן does not prove that a voluntary עולה gets שירה. The words were a lament, and songs may be said on the דוכן even without an offering.

steps.title: So what is the final answer?
steps.stepSummary: The proof from the story was pushed off, so the גמרא asks what the conclusion is about a voluntary עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What came of it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. Since the proof failed, it asks how the question about שירה for a voluntary עולה is actually settled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every proof so far has been pushed aside, so the question is still open. The גמרא now looks for a real source that decides it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What came of it?' Asking for the final answer to an open question
A communal burnt offering, brought for the whole people
An open question that is waiting for an answer

phrases.english: What came of it?
phrases.notes: 'It' is the open question: does a communal voluntary עולה get שירה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof in steps 23 to 27 fell apart, the גמרא goes back to the original question
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a communal voluntary עולה is accompanied by שירה

steps.title: A פסוק links עולות and שלמים
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי בריה דרב כהנא brings the פסוק 'על עלתיכם ועל זבחי שלמיכם', which puts עולות and שלמים side by side.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב מרי, son of רב כהנא, taught: 'Over your burnt offerings and over the sacrifices of your peace offerings.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to answer the question. It is a פסוק about blowing trumpets over the offerings, and it mentions עולות and שלמים together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the פסוק names עולות and שלמים next to each other, we compare them. Whatever is true of one kind is true of the other kind for this rule. That also tells us which offerings get שירה. The next step spells out what the comparison teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
Peace offerings, which are partly eaten
A comparison learned from two things placed together in one פסוק

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא:
phrases.english: Come and hear, for רב מרי, son of רב כהנא, taught:
'Over your burnt offerings and over the sacrifices of your peace offerings.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 10:10. That פסוק is about blowing trumpets over the offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source that answers the question of step 32
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A פסוק that compares עולות to שלמים, which will set limits on which עולות get שירה

steps.title: Only a fixed-time עולה gets שירה
steps.stepSummary: The comparison works both ways. The שלמים must be קדשי קדשים like the עולה, and the עולה must have a fixed time like the שלמים. So a voluntary עולה does not get שירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as an עולה is קדשי קדשים, so too the שלמים here are קדשי קדשים. And just as these שלמים have a set time, so too the עולה must have a set time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws two lessons from the comparison. These lessons narrow down which offerings get שירה, and the result leaves out the voluntary עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First lesson: the שלמים that get שירה must be קדשי קדשים like an עולה. The only שלמים of that kind are the lambs brought with the two loaves on שבועות. Second lesson: since those שלמים have a set time, the עולה that gets שירה must also have a set time. A voluntary עולה has no set time, so it gets no שירה.

keyTerms.meaning: The most holy class of offerings
Has a set, fixed time to be brought
The two lambs brought as שלמים with the two loaves on שבועות
'Just as… so too…' The form used for drawing a comparison

steps.whatToRemember: A communal voluntary עולה does not get שירה. The פסוק compares עולה to שלמים, and the only שלמים that count have a set time, so only a fixed-time עולה gets שירה.
steps.confusionAlert: The comparison runs in both directions. The עולה teaches about the שלמים (they must be קדשי קדשים), and the שלמים teach about the עולה (it must have a set time).
steps.whyThisMatters: This finally settles רבי אבין's question, which the proofs from חזקיהו and from the story of the חורבן could not decide: שירה goes only with an עולה that has a set time.

phrases.english: Just as a burnt offering is of the most holy class,
so too the peace offerings here are of the most holy class,
and just as these peace offerings have a set time,
so too the burnt offering must have a set time.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה עוֹלָה קוֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים — אַף שְׁלָמִים קוֹדֶשׁ קֳדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out what the פסוק in step 33 teaches
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Only an עולה with a set time gets שירה, so a communal voluntary עולה is not accompanied by שירה.
